# Hellesylt flora, treeline and harbour: research notes

Scope: read-only web research. No repository files were edited. Hellesylt-specific figures were often not found, and this is stated where it applies.

## 1. Treeline

- Geirangerfjord area (older datasheet): tree line on the mountains at 900 m and 1,100 m; alpine vegetation from about 1,300-1,400 m. Source: http://www.yichuans.me/datasheet/output/site/west-norwegian-fjords-geirangerfjord-and-naeroyfjord/
- UNESCO nomination: alpine vegetation extends from treeline to 1,400 m; the highest point above the fjord is Torvløysa at 1,850 m. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/document/152008
- Norway-wide: forest line on the southern and western coast is 500-600 m, reaching 1,200 m in places; treeline is usually 20-30 m above the forest line; birch most often forms it. Source: https://snl.no/tregrense
- Sunnmøre: forest limit runs from sea level at the outer coast to over 800 m inland (MET avalanche-warning wiki; approximate). Source: https://wiki.met.no/snoskred/varsling/sunnmore
- Hellesylt-specific treeline: **not found**. The inner-fjord position suggests a value at the higher end of the coastal range, but no source quantifies it.

## 2. Vegetation by zone

- **Valley floor and fjord slopes:** birch is the dominant tree on fjord slopes in Sunnmøre surveys, with aspen, elm and hazel, and rich hazel scrub (rikt hasselkratt) is listed as a threatened type. Source (Hjørundfjorden survey): https://www.hjorundfjord.no/artikkel/2008/02/kartlagde-naturtypar-langs-hjorundfjorden. Hellesylt survey: not found. Spruce and pine plantations: not found.
- **Grassland and hay meadow:** the Geiranger-Herdalen survey (Norddal and Stranda) mainly records grazed semi-natural pasture. Source: https://www.statsforvalteren.no/siteassets/fm-more-og-romsdal/dokument-fmmr/naturvern/kartleggingsrapporter/naturtypekartlegging-2016_geiranger_herdalen.pdf. Species list not retrieved.
- **Heath above treeline:** coastal heaths in Norway are confined to the highly oceanic section (O3). Calluna vulgaris is usually dominant. Empetrum nigrum's share rises northward. Calluna responds to burning, Empetrum does not, and western Norway burns every 25-50 years. Source: https://ntnuopen.ntnu.no/ntnu-xmlui/bitstream/handle/11250/244613/124859_FULLTEXT01.pdf . Vaccinium cover and heights: not found in sources.
- **Latin species names and typical heights** for the valley and meadow zones were not found in the sources retrieved.

## 3. Hellesylt harbour layout

- A floating quay is being installed at the end of the ferry quay and molo for the small-boat harbour, north of the quay house (kaihuset). It was due to be ready for the 2026 summer season. Dimensions and material: not found. Source: https://www.hellesylt.info/2025/12/flytande-kaianlegg-pa-hellesylt/
- Stranda hamnevesen KF has taken over the Hellesylt ferry quay. Source: https://www.stranda-hamnevesen.no/no/stranda-hamnevesen-kf-tek-over-ferjekaiene-pa-hellesylt-og-i-geiranger/
- The ferry quay move across the river was planned for years. The sources name the **Langedalselva**, not the Hellesyltelva. Source: https://www.hellesylt.info/2021/08/vedtok-utgreiing-av-ny-ferjekai-pa-hellesylt/
- A breakwater west of the ferry quay near the river mouth is **not confirmed**. The sources place the molo at the ferry quay and small-boat harbour, north of the quay house, which conflicts with the premise.
- Sizes, coordinates and stone or concrete material: not found. Kartverket and norgeskart were not consulted.

## 4. Slope threshold

- Snow avalanche release is usually at 30-50° (NVE 2014). Source: https://publikasjoner.nve.no/veileder/2014/veileder2014_08.pdf
- Rockfall release: NVE 2014 gives steeper than 40-45°; NVE 2021 gives steeper than 60-70°. The figures are context-dependent. Source: https://publikasjoner.nve.no/rapport/2021/rapport2021_20.pdf
- A Sykkylven fjordside example is about 30° near sea level and over 45° higher up. Source: https://www.sykkylven.kommune.no/_f/p1/i49afbcb2-7e4b-4ef7-9b31-a9bfeda2d9ae/rapport-skredfarevurdering-roneset.pdf
- A bare-rock or vegetation threshold angle: **not found**. NGU notes that unvegetated slopes can release soil slides at lower gradients. Source: https://static.ngu.no/FileArchive/235/2006_043.pdf
